key_insight: Physics-informed neural networks identify plate orientations for near-isotropic, ultrastiff closed-cell lattices, with at least six plates required.
engineering_relevance: These architectures offer a route to lightweight structures with high stiffness and nearly direction-independent mechanical response.
method: Use PINNs to solve analytical equations for plate orientations.
Assemble orientations into quasi-random foam-like geometries and validate with finite element simulations.
Additively manufacture six-plate lattices using LAPIS and characterize experimentally.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 90% of the Hashin–Shtrikman stiffness upper bound at relative density 0.4 and a near-isotropic Zener ratio of 0.95 at relative density 0.1.
watch_item: Suboptimal plate placement introduces bending, limiting how closely realized lattices approach the theoretical stiffness bound.
paper_title: Derivation of Novel Isotropic Metamaterials at the Hashin Shtrikman Stiffness Limit Enabled by Physics Informed Neural Networks
